tldr: The system is choosing to hold off on any Amazon (AMZN) trade today. The stock has been on a powerful upward run, but the price is too stretched and there is no clean entry point — entering now would mean chasing a move that is already mostly over. The system is patiently waiting for either a pullback to a better price level or a confirmed breakout above key resistance before acting.
narrative:
Amazon's stock has been on a tear. After a blowout earnings report in late April, the share price surged from around $209 to over $272, a gain of more than 30% in just a few weeks. That kind of move is impressive, but it also creates a problem for traders trying to enter now: the best entries are already gone.

All five swing-trading strategy agents looked at AMZN today and reached the same conclusion — neutral. This is a rare unanimous agreement, but it is not a disagreement about direction. Most agents actually believe the underlying trend is healthy and legitimate. Bulls absorbed a major resistance zone (the $268-$276 range where a prior short-trade was stopped out on May 4), which is a sign of genuine buying strength. The trend is real.

The tension is this: the stock is in an extreme overbought zone (think of it as a rubber band stretched very far from its resting point), and recent volume has been unusually thin on the hourly charts. The system tried a short trade (betting the stock would fall) just yesterday, and got stopped out at a loss of $10.14. That failure is an important lesson baked into today's analysis — the system explicitly notes it will not repeat the same bearish bet without fresh confirmation.

What would tip the balance? Two clear scenarios were identified. First, if AMZN pulls back to around $258-$265 (the 10-day moving average zone, essentially the stock's recent 'baseline') with the momentum indicators cooling down, that is a clean long entry with an attractive risk-reward ratio of about 3.5-to-1. Second, if the stock decisively closes above the $276 resistance level on heavy volume, that would signal a breakout worth buying into, targeting $296. Neither setup is available today.

The fundamental picture adds a layer of complexity. The growth and financial health signals are solid — earnings grew 31% and the company carries very little debt relative to its size. However, the valuation analysis is firmly bearish: by traditional models like discounted cash flow (a method that estimates what all future profits are worth in today's dollars), the stock is trading at roughly 47% above its estimated fair value. That is expensive. The system weighs both sides and lands on patience.

AMZN.verdict: The system recommends holding — no trade today — with 52% confidence, as the stock lacks a valid entry point after a massive run-up and a recent failed short trade.
AMZN.bull_case: The bull case for Amazon is structurally strong. The trend is confirmed and powerful: the moving averages are perfectly aligned (short-term above medium-term above long-term), and the ADX trend-strength indicator is at an extreme 65.1, signaling one of the strongest uptrends in the market. The Q1 2026 earnings report was historic — earnings per share came in at $2.78 versus a consensus estimate of $1.64, a 69.5% beat. AWS cloud revenue grew 28% year-over-year. Fundamentals back it up too: revenue is growing at 12%, earnings at 31%, and the company has very low debt (debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17). The swing_trend_momentum and swing_breakout agents are both optimistic about the underlying thesis and are simply waiting for a better price. If AMZN pulls back to the $258-$265 zone, the trend-momentum agent would target $284.65 with a favorable 3.5-to-1 risk-reward ratio.
AMZN.bear_case: The bear case is about price exhaustion, not business quality. RSI (a momentum meter on a 0-100 scale, where above 70 signals overbought) stands at 80.49 on the standard 14-day reading and an alarming 90.43 on the 21-day reading — both deep in overbought territory. The stock is trading 20.4% above its 50-day moving average (a long-term trend line), and a statistical measure called the Z-score is at 2.06, meaning the price is more than 2 standard deviations above where it 'should' be. The valuation model finds the stock roughly 47% above its DCF-estimated fair value of approximately $1.55 trillion versus its current market cap of $2.94 trillion. Additionally, on the hourly chart, volume has nearly dried up (relative volume 0.04x vs normal), suggesting the recent price stability near $272 may be drifting, not supported. The prior short trade was stopped out at $276 on May 4, but that same $276 level has not been decisively broken — it remains active resistance.

key_numbers.ADX 65.1: ADX (Average Directional Index) measures trend strength on a scale of 0-100. Above 25 is a trend; above 50 is very strong; 65.1 is exceptional. High is good if you already own the stock, but it also means the move is mature and late entrants face higher risk.
key_numbers.RSI-14 at 80.49 / RSI-21 at 90.43: RSI (Relative Strength Index) measures how fast and far a stock has moved relative to recent history. Above 70 is considered overbought — like a sprint runner running out of breath. At 80-90, the stock is historically likely to pause or pull back at some point. High RSI is a caution flag for new buyers.
key_numbers.Price 20.4% above 50-day SMA: The 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) is an average of the stock's price over the last 50 trading days — think of it as the stock's 'fair value highway.' Being 20% above it is like driving 80mph in a 50mph zone. The car can keep going, but it is running hot.
key_numbers.P/E Ratio 32.76: P/E (Price-to-Earnings Ratio) tells you how much investors pay for each $1 of the company's profits. At 32.76, investors pay $32.76 for every $1 AMZN earns annually. The average S&P 500 P/E is roughly 20-22, so AMZN carries a significant premium — justified by growth expectations, but leaves less margin for error.
key_numbers.DCF Gap -47.4%: The DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) model estimates what a company is intrinsically worth based on all its projected future profits. A -47.4% gap means the current market price is 47% higher than this estimate — in other words, the stock may already be pricing in a lot of optimistic future growth. If growth disappoints, the stock has room to fall significantly.
key_numbers.Risk-Reward conditional entries: The system identifies two future entry scenarios: a long at $262 targeting $284.65 (stop $256) gives a 3.5-to-1 ratio — meaning for every $1 risked, you could gain $3.50. A breakout long at $276.50 targeting $296 (stop $268) gives a 2.3-to-1 ratio. Neither is available today.

AMZN.risk_summary: The primary risks in order of likelihood: (1) Overbought snapback — at RSI 90+ and Z-score 2.06, a sharp pullback to the 10-day EMA zone around $258-$265 is entirely normal and would be healthy, but could be unpleasant for anyone who buys today. (2) Macro left-tail — the Iran-UAE / Strait of Hormuz conflict is unresolved, with oil above $102 per barrel. A sudden escalation could hit high-growth tech stocks hard and fast. (3) Fed leadership risk — a hawkish new Fed chair succeeding to power around May 15 could reset interest rate expectations, which tend to compress expensive tech valuations. (4) Recurrence of the stop-out pattern — the system's own track record shows two consecutive stop-outs (AMZN short May 4 and NVDA long April 30) in high-RSI, high-ADX regimes, with a 0% win rate on EMA-pullback setups over the last 30 days. This is an explicit pattern warning. (5) Valuation ceiling — with the stock already trading 47% above DCF fair value and facing $200B in AI capex scrutiny from analysts, any earnings miss or guidance cut would be severely punished.

concepts.Swing Trading: A style of trading where you hold a position for 2 to 20 days (not buying and holding forever, and not buying and selling within one day). You are trying to capture a 'swing' — a short-to-medium-term move up or down. Today's system is running in swing mode.
concepts.Hold (action): In swing trading context, 'hold' means the system is not opening any new position today. If you already own the stock, you keep it; if you don't own it, you stay out and watch. It is not a buy or sell signal.
concepts.Entry Price: The price at which the system would open a trade. Think of it as the 'buy alarm' — if conditions are right and the stock reaches this level, that is when the system thinks it is a good moment to act.
concepts.Target Price: The price the system aims to exit the trade for a profit. This is the 'goal line.' The system calculates this using technical chart levels, Fibonacci extensions, and measured moves.
concepts.Stop Loss: A predetermined price at which the system would exit the trade to limit losses if the stock moves against expectations. Think of it as a fire exit — you use it to get out safely before things get worse.
concepts.Risk-Reward Ratio: A comparison of potential gain versus potential loss. A 3:1 risk-reward ratio means for every $1 you could lose (distance to stop), you could gain $3 (distance to target). Higher is better; the system generally requires at least 2:1 to consider a trade worth taking.
concepts.ADX (Average Directional Index): A technical indicator that measures how strong a trend is, regardless of direction. Ranges 0-100. Below 25 = no real trend (choppy). Above 50 = very strong trend. At 65.1, AMZN is in an exceptionally strong trend.
concepts.RSI (Relative Strength Index): A momentum indicator measuring how overbought or oversold a stock is, on a 0-100 scale. Above 70 = overbought (stock has risen fast, may be due for a pause). Below 30 = oversold (stock has fallen fast, may be due for a bounce). AMZN is at 80-90, which is deeply overbought.
concepts.EMA (Exponential Moving Average): An average of past prices that gives more weight to recent prices. The 10 EMA is a short-term trend line (last ~10 days), the 21 EMA is medium-term, and the 50 EMA is long-term. When short-term EMAs are above long-term EMAs ('EMA alignment'), the trend is bullish.
concepts.Z-Score: A statistical measure of how far a value is from its average, measured in standard deviations. A Z-score of 2.0 means the stock is 2 standard deviations above its normal price — statistically extreme. Historically, stocks tend to revert toward their average over time.
concepts.Bollinger %B: A percentage measuring where the current price sits within its Bollinger Bands (statistical price channels). 0% = at the lower band, 100% = at the upper band. At 0.86 (86%), AMZN is near the top of its normal range — meaning it is stretched relative to recent history.
concepts.DCF (Discounted Cash Flow): A valuation model that estimates what a company is worth today by projecting all future profits and discounting them back to present value. It is the 'fundamental fair value' estimate. If the market price is far above DCF value, the stock may be expensive.
concepts.P/E Ratio (Price-to-Earnings): How much investors pay per dollar of annual earnings. P/E of 32.76 means investors pay $32.76 for every $1 of AMZN's profits. Higher P/E can be justified by faster growth but leaves less room for error.
concepts.Relative Volume: Today's trading volume compared to the average volume. A relative volume of 1.0x means normal activity. 0.04x on the hourly chart means almost no one is trading — the market is quiet, which can signal conviction is low behind recent price moves.
concepts.Fibonacci Extension / Retracement: Fibonacci levels are mathematical ratios (23.6%, 38.2%, 61.8%, etc.) that traders use to identify likely support and resistance price levels. Extensions project where a stock might go after a breakout; retracements identify pullback targets. They are widely watched, making them somewhat self-fulfilling.
concepts.Support and Resistance: Support is a price level where buying has historically stepped in to stop a decline (like a floor). Resistance is a price level where selling has historically capped advances (like a ceiling). $276 is a key resistance level for AMZN right now.
concepts.Overbought: A stock is considered overbought when it has risen so far, so fast, that statistical and momentum indicators suggest it is due for a rest or pullback. It does not mean the stock will definitely fall — trends can persist — but risk is elevated for new buyers.
concepts.WACC (Weighted Average Cost of Capital): The minimum return a company needs to earn to satisfy all its investors (debt holders and stockholders). Used in DCF models as the discount rate. AMZN's WACC is estimated at 10.7%.
concepts.Debt-to-Equity Ratio: A measure of financial leverage — how much debt a company has relative to shareholders' equity. AMZN's D/E of 0.17 is very low, meaning the company is mostly funded by equity, not debt. Low is generally healthier and safer.
concepts.Conviction / Confidence Level: A percentage estimate of how certain the system is about its analysis. 52% confidence means the system is only slightly more sure than a coin flip — meaningful uncertainty exists. Higher confidence (70%+) suggests stronger conviction.
